title: Dataset of intracranial EEG during cortical stimulation evoking visual effects
description: This dataset comprises intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 22 patients undergoing stereo-EEG presurgical evaluation for drug-resistant epilepsy, capturing responses to 115 high-frequency cortical stimulations that evoked visual hallucinations. Each recording includes 21 seconds of iEEG data surrounding each stimulation event, with detailed annotations of stimulation parameters and 14 categories of evoked clinical visual phenomena. The dataset supports investigation of brain networks underlying stimulation-evoked visual symptoms and enables construction of symptom-related activation and connectivity maps.
methods_description: High-frequency bipolar intracranial stimulations were delivered using alternating polarity biphasic pulses of 1 ms duration at 43.2 Hz or 50 Hz, with current intensities between 0.25 and 3 mA, for up to 5 seconds. The alternating polarity protocol was used to disambiguate neuronal responses time-locked to stimulation from artefactual components. Recordings span 8 seconds before stimulation onset, the stimulation period (up to 5 s), and 8 seconds after stimulation offset. Stimulation contact pairs, current intensity, and evoked clinical effects were documented in accompanying events files.
